fullPassage:
Hello, listeners. Did you know there are times at night when a massive migration happens right over your heads? The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in conservation efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr. Weidensaul.
Thanks for having me, Jo.
Your new book says every spring and fall, hundreds of millions to billions of migratory birds pass over our roofs, but we seem to have no idea that it's happening. Why is that?
Well, most birds migrate after dark, including almost all of the birds that are normally active during the day. That's why it's hard for us to realize the migration is happening. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer predators at night. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
Among those global travelers in your book, I found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly impressive.
Sure. Some of them can even make a 10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days.
How do they travel such a long distance over a nearly featureless ocean?
To find their routes, the bar-tailed godwits probably rely on the sun and stars among other things. Some experts believe that they may be able to sense the earth's magnetic field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if ever, they sleep while flying over a vast ocean. It turns out that migratory birds use an approach called "half-brain sleep." This is how it works. Only the left half of the brain sleeps for a couple of seconds, then only the right half for the next couple of seconds, and then this process repeats over and over again. Isn't it amazing? Actually, some sea mammals like dolphins can do that, too, because they have to keep breathing consciously.
That's a neat trick. Who wouldn't like to have such an ability?
Birds in migratory condition can do things that they can't do at other times of the year. Another neat trick you might envy is that they can gain a tremendous amount of muscle tissue without exercise. For example, before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific, they undergo a process of binge feeding. They just eat and eat until they double their weight. By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can and can't put any more weight on, their digestive organs shrink dramatically because these won't be put to use during the non-stop flight to New Zealand.
Then what happens after they arrive there?
They regrow their digestive organs and spend the summer feeding again, and they undergo the same journey back to Alaska. They do this again and again for 25 to 30 years, flying up to 30,000 km every year. By the time bar-tailed godwits die, they have flown close to twice the distance from Earth to the moon.
That's truly impressive. By the way, I hear you've visited Korea several times before. Why do you come here so often?
As a bird watcher and conservationist, I find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and China very special. They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a critical stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms.
So the mudflats are drawing all kinds of birds in from as far away as New Zealand, Australia, and Asia?
Yes. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks and make another flight of several thousand kilometers up north. That's why the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It's one of the few places in the world where migratory birds can get the resources they need on their difficult journey.
Oh, I had no idea that the Yellow Sea has such importance. What do you think we can do to preserve this precious gathering place for migratory birds?
Well, you can start by raising awareness of its importance among people around you. Or, if you want to be more actively involved, you can participate in cleaning up beaches or monitoring wildlife habitats. On a bigger scale, because migratory birds travel through many countries, international cooperation is a must for their protection. Actually, I'm working with an international organization consisting of the countries along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. As a result of our international collaboration, we managed to successfully bring back the endangered black-faced spoonbills.
Fascinating! Mr. Weidensaul, today you let us see migratory birds and the Yellow Sea in a whole new way. Thank you!

questions.passage: The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite (A)[naturalist / nationalist] and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent (B)[decades / moments] studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in (C)[conservation / conversation] efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr. Weidensaul.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 자연주의자(naturalist)이자 작가인 Scott Weidensaul을 초대하여 지식을 나누고자 한다. 그는 수십 년간(decades) 철새를 연구하고 보전(conservation) 활동에 참여해왔다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① naturalist — decades — conservation: 원문 일치. 자연주의자가 수십 년간 새를 연구하며 보전 활동에 참여
❌ ② nationalist(국가주의자): 새를 연구하는 사람이므로 naturalist가 적절
❌ ③ moments(순간들): '수십 년'이 원문이므로 moments는 부적절
❌ ④ conversation(대화): conservation(보전)과 혼동 주의. 새 보호 맥락에서 conservation이 적절
det.tip: naturalist(자연주의자) ↔ nationalist(국가주의자), decades(수십 년) ↔ moments(순간), conservation(보전) ↔ conversation(대화)

questions.passage: Well, most birds migrate after dark, including almost all of the birds that are normally active during the day. That's why it's hard for us to realize the migration is happening. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer (A)[predators / protectors] at night. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything (B)[visible / invisible], this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural (C)[spectacle / obstacle] on the planet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 밤에는 포식자(predators)가 더 적다. 밤하늘을 벗기고 모든 것을 보이게(visible) 만들 수 있다면, 이 이동은 지구상 가장 큰 자연 장관(spectacle)일 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② predators — visible — spectacle: 원문 일치. 포식자가 적은 밤에 이동하고, 보이게 만들면 장관이라는 맥락
❌ ① invisible(보이지 않는): 이미 보이지 않는데 invisible로 만드는 것은 모순
❌ ③ protectors(보호자): 밤에 보호자가 적다는 맥락이 부자연스러움
❌ ④ obstacle(장애물): 자연의 경이로움을 표현하므로 spectacle이 적절
det.tip: predator(포식자) ↔ protector(보호자), visible(보이는) ↔ invisible(보이지 않는), spectacle(장관) ↔ obstacle(장애물)

questions.passage: Birds in migratory condition can do things that they can't do at other times of the year. Another neat trick you might envy is that they can gain a (A)[tremendous / trivial] amount of muscle tissue without exercise. For example, before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific, they (B)[undergo / overlook] a process of binge feeding. They just eat and eat until they double their weight. By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can, their digestive organs (C)[shrink / expand] dramatically.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 운동 없이 엄청난(tremendous) 양의 근육 조직을 얻을 수 있다. 폭식 과정을 겪는다(undergo). 소화 기관이 극적으로 줄어든다(shrink).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ tremendous — undergo — shrink: 원문 일치. 엄청난 근육 증가 → 폭식 과정 겪음 → 소화기관 축소
❌ ① overlook(간과하다): 과정을 '겪는' 것이므로 undergo가 적절
❌ ② trivial(사소한): 엄청난 양이라는 맥락이므로 tremendous가 적절
❌ ④ expand(확장하다): 비행 중 소화기관을 쓰지 않으므로 shrink가 적절
det.tip: tremendous(엄청난) ↔ trivial(사소한), undergo(겪다) ↔ overlook(간과하다), shrink(줄어들다) ↔ expand(확장하다)

questions.passage: The scale of migration involving ①<u>billions</u> of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in ②<u>awe</u>. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying ③<u>migratory</u> birds, writing about them, and engaging in ④<u>destruction</u> efforts. Welcome to the show, Mr. Weidensaul.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 보전(conservation) 활동에 참여해왔다. ④ destruction(파괴)은 conservation(보전)과 반대이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ destruction → conservation(보전): 새를 연구하고 보호하는 사람이므로 conservation이 원문. destruction(파괴)은 반대
❌ ① billions(수십억): 원문 그대로. 수십억 마리의 새
❌ ② awe(경외): 원문 그대로. 이동 규모에 경외감
❌ ③ migratory(철새의): 원문 그대로. 철새를 연구
det.tip: conservation(보전/보호) ↔ destruction(파괴). engage in conservation efforts = 보전 활동에 참여하다

questions.passage: To find their routes, the bar-tailed godwits probably ①<u>rely on</u> the sun and stars among other things. Some experts believe that they may be able to ②<u>sense</u> the earth's magnetic field lines, too. You may also wonder how, if ever, they sleep while flying over a ③<u>vast</u> ocean. It turns out that migratory birds use an approach called "half-brain sleep." Only the left half of the brain sleeps for a couple of seconds, then only the right half for the next couple of seconds, and then this process ④<u>ceases</u> over and over again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 과정이 계속해서 반복된다(repeats). ① ceases(멈추다)는 repeats(반복되다)와 반대이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ vast(광활한): 원문 그대로. 광활한 대양
❌ ① rely on(~에 의존하다): 원문 그대로. 태양과 별에 의존
❌ ② sense(감지하다): 원문 그대로. 자기장을 감지
✅ ④ ceases → repeats(반복되다): 'over and over again'(계속해서)과 함께 쓰이므로 repeats가 원문. ceases(멈추다)는 반복의 반대
det.tip: repeat(반복하다) ↔ cease(멈추다/중단하다). 'over and over again'은 반복을 나타내는 표현이므로 repeats와 자연스럽게 연결됨

questions.passage: As a bird watcher and conservationist, I find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and China very special. They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a ①<u>critical</u> stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look ②<u>featureless</u> to the human eye, they have ③<u>plenty</u> of marine life forms. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. That's why the Yellow Sea is so ④<u>marginally</u> important.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 황해가 매우 결정적으로(critically) 중요하다. ④ marginally(미미하게)는 critically(결정적으로)와 반대이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ marginally → critically(결정적으로): 원문은 'so critically important'. 황해가 철새에게 매우 중요하다는 맥락에서 marginally(미미하게)는 부적절
❌ ① critical(중요한): 원문 그대로. 중요한 중간 기착지
❌ ② featureless(특징 없는): 원문 그대로. 인간의 눈에는 특징 없어 보이지만
❌ ③ plenty(풍부한): 원문 그대로. 풍부한 해양 생물
det.tip: critically(결정적으로/매우) ↔ marginally(미미하게/근소하게). critically important = 매우 중요한. marginally important = 별로 중요하지 않은

questions.passage: Hello, listeners. Did you know there are times at night when a __________ migration happens right over your heads? The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in conservation efforts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밤에 대규모(massive) 이동이 바로 여러분의 머리 위에서 일어난다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② massive(대규모의): billions of birds(수십억 마리)와 thousands of kilometers(수천 킬로미터)로 이동의 규모가 엄청남
❌ ① subtle(미묘한): 수십억 마리의 이동이 '미묘한'은 모순
❌ ③ occasional(가끔의): 매년 봄가을 정기적으로 일어나는 이동
❌ ④ fictional(허구의): 실제 일어나는 현상이므로 부적절
det.tip: massive = 대규모의, 거대한. 수량(billions)과 거리(thousands of km)가 단서. subtle = 미묘한, occasional = 가끔의

questions.passage: Birds in migratory condition can do things that they can't do at other times of the year. Another neat trick you might envy is that they can gain a tremendous amount of muscle tissue without exercise. For example, before some bar-tailed godwits leave Alaska in September and make a 10,000 km flight across the Pacific, they undergo a process of __________. They just eat and eat until they double their weight.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 폭식(binge feeding) 과정을 거친다. 그들은 체중이 두 배가 될 때까지 먹고 또 먹는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① binge feeding(폭식): 'eat and eat until they double their weight'가 직접적 설명. 체중이 두 배가 될 때까지 먹는 행위
❌ ② strict fasting(엄격한 단식): 먹고 또 먹는다는 내용과 반대
❌ ③ gentle exercise(가벼운 운동): 본문은 운동 없이(without exercise) 근육을 얻는다고 했음
❌ ④ slow migration(느린 이동): 문맥상 먹는 과정이지 이동 과정이 아님
det.tip: binge = 폭식, 과도한. binge feeding = 폭식. 'eat and eat until they double their weight'가 binge feeding의 구체적 설명

questions.passage: As a bird watcher and conservationist, I find the Yellow Sea mudflats between Korea and China very special. They are some of the largest tidal mudflats on the earth and provide a critical stopover point for the countless migratory birds on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway. While these enormous stretches of tidal mud look featureless to the human eye, they have plenty of marine life forms. Many of these birds fly several thousand kilometers to get to the Yellow Sea. Here, they have to double their weight in less than two weeks and make another flight of several thousand kilometers up north. That's why the Yellow Sea is so critically important. It's one of the few places in the world where migratory birds can get the __________ they need on their difficult journey.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 철새들이 힘든 여정에서 필요한 자원(resources)을 얻을 수 있는 세계 몇 안 되는 장소이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ resources(자원): 체중을 두 배로 늘려야 하는 철새에게 먹이 등의 자원이 필요하다는 맥락
❌ ① obstacles(장애물): 여정에서 필요한 것이 장애물이라는 것은 모순
❌ ② predators(포식자): 포식자가 필요하다는 것은 비논리적
❌ ④ spectacles(장관): 여정에 필요한 것이 장관이라는 것은 문맥에 맞지 않음
det.tip: resources = 자원, 식량. critically important + get the resources they need = 필요한 자원을 얻다. 철새가 체중을 두 배로 늘리기 위한 풍부한 먹이가 핵심

questions.passage: Did you know there are times at night when a massive migration happens right over your heads? The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in <u>awe</u>. On today's Jo's Tea Time, we invite naturalist and author Scott Weidensaul to share his knowledge. He's spent decades studying migratory birds, writing about them, and engaging in conservation efforts.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>awe</u>와 가장 가까운 의미의 단어는?

det.korean: awe = 경외감, 경이(wonder). 수십억 마리의 새가 수천 km를 이동하는 규모에 경이로움을 느낀다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ wonder(경이): awe는 경외감, 놀라움으로 wonder와 유사
❌ ① anger(분노): 경외감과 무관
❌ ② boredom(지루함): 경외감의 반대에 가까움
❌ ③ confusion(혼란): 경외감과 다른 감정
det.tip: awe = wonder = amazement (경외감, 경이). 'in awe' = 경외감에 빠져. leaves you in awe = 경외감을 느끼게 한다

questions.passage: Among those global travelers in your book, I found the bar-tailed godwits to be particularly <u>impressive</u>. Sure. Some of them can even make a 10,000 km non-stop journey across the Pacific Ocean, from western Alaska to New Zealand in 11 days.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>impressive</u>와 가장 가까운 의미의 단어는?

det.korean: impressive = 인상적인, 놀라운(remarkable). 10,000km 논스톱 비행이 인상적이라는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① remarkable(놀라운/주목할 만한): impressive와 유의어. 비범한 업적을 표현
❌ ② ordinary(평범한): impressive의 반의어
❌ ③ insignificant(하찮은): impressive의 반의어
❌ ④ trivial(사소한): impressive의 반의어
det.tip: impressive = remarkable = striking = outstanding (인상적인, 놀라운). 모두 '뛰어나서 놀라운'이라는 의미

questions.passage: Well, you can start by raising awareness of its importance among people around you. Or, if you want to be more actively involved, you can participate in cleaning up beaches or monitoring wildlife <u>habitats</u>. On a bigger scale, because migratory birds travel through many countries, international cooperation is a must for their protection.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>habitats</u>와 가장 가까운 의미의 단어는?

det.korean: habitats = 서식지, 환경(environments). 야생동물의 서식지를 모니터링한다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ② environments(환경): habitats(서식지)와 가장 유사. 생물이 사는 자연환경
❌ ① habits(습관): habitats와 철자가 비슷하지만 의미가 전혀 다름
❌ ③ obstacles(장애물): 서식지와 무관한 의미
❌ ④ migrations(이동): 서식지가 아닌 이동을 의미
det.tip: habitat(서식지) ≠ habit(습관). 철자 혼동 주의! habitat = 동식물이 사는 자연환경 = natural environment

questions.passage: As a result of our international collaboration, we managed to successfully bring back the <u>endangered</u> black-faced spoonbills. Fascinating! Mr. Weidensaul, today you let us see migratory birds and the Yellow Sea in a whole new way.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>endangered</u>와 가장 반대되는 의미의 단어는?

det.korean: endangered = 멸종 위기의. 반의어: thriving(번성하는).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ thriving(번성하는): endangered(멸종 위기의)의 반의어. 개체수가 풍부하고 잘 살고 있는 상태
❌ ① threatened(위협받는): endangered와 유의어. 반의어가 아님
❌ ② vulnerable(취약한): endangered와 유사한 의미. 반의어가 아님
❌ ④ extinct(멸종된): endangered보다 더 심각한 상태. 반의어가 아님
det.tip: endangered(멸종 위기) ↔ thriving(번성하는). threatened/vulnerable은 유의어. extinct(멸종)은 더 심각한 단계

questions.passage: By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can and can't put any more weight on, their digestive organs <u>shrink</u> dramatically because these won't be put to use during the non-stop flight to New Zealand. Then what happens after they arrive there? They regrow their digestive organs and spend the summer feeding again, and they undergo the same journey back to Alaska.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>shrink</u>와 가장 반대되는 의미의 단어는?

det.korean: shrink = 줄어들다. 반의어: expand(확장하다/팽창하다).
det.analysis:
✅ ② expand(확장하다): shrink(줄어들다)의 정확한 반의어. 크기가 커지다
❌ ① contract(수축하다): shrink와 유의어. 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ reduce(줄이다): shrink와 유의어. 반의어가 아님
❌ ④ diminish(감소하다): shrink와 유의어. 반의어가 아님
det.tip: shrink = contract = reduce = diminish (줄어들다). 반의어: expand = grow = enlarge (커지다)

questions.passage: The scale of migration involving billions of birds traveling up to thousands of kilometers leaves you in awe. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
questions.stem: 'scale'이 다음 글에서 쓰인 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?
ch: She stepped on the scale to check her weight.
The fish has shiny silver scales.
The scale of the disaster was beyond imagination.
He learned to play the C major scale on the piano.

det.korean: 본문의 scale = 규모. 수십억 마리의 새가 이동하는 '규모'를 의미한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ scale = 규모: 재난의 규모(The scale of the disaster)와 같은 의미. 이동의 규모
❌ ① scale = 저울: 체중을 재는 도구
❌ ② scales = 비늘: 물고기의 비늘
❌ ③ scale = 음계: 피아노 음계
det.tip: scale의 다의어: ① 규모(the scale of ~) ② 저울(on the scale) ③ 비늘(fish scales) ④ 음계(musical scale)

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어를 고르시오.

"a place where a person or animal stops for a short time during a journey"

det.korean: stopover = 중간 기착지. 여행 중 잠시 멈추는 장소.
det.analysis:
✅ ① stopover(중간 기착지): 'a place where one stops for a short time during a journey'의 정확한 정의
❌ ② spectacle(장관): 눈에 띄는 볼거리
❌ ③ obstacle(장애물): 방해하는 것
❌ ④ habitat(서식지): 동식물이 사는 자연환경
det.tip: stopover = layover = transit point (중간 기착지). 본문에서 'a critical stopover point'로 사용됨

questions.passage: Well, you can start by raising awareness of its importance among people around you. Or, if you want to be more actively involved, you can participate in cleaning up beaches or monitoring wildlife habitats. On a bigger scale, because migratory birds travel through many countries, international [cooperate] is a must for their protection.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형을 변환하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 국제적 협력(cooperation)은 그들의 보호를 위해 반드시 필요하다. cooperate(동사) → cooperation(명사).
det.analysis: international + [명사] 구조. cooperate(동사: 협력하다) → cooperation(명사: 협력). 'is a must'의 주어 자리이므로 명사가 필요.
det.tip: cooperate(동사) → cooperation(명사). collaborate(동사) → collaboration(명사). 동사에서 명사로 바꿀 때 -tion/-sion 접미사 활용

questions.passage: By the time they take off, their heart and flight muscles may have increased by 50%. After they have eaten as much as they possibly can and can't put any more weight on, their digestive organs shrink dramatically because these won't be put to use during the non-stop flight to New Zealand. Then what happens after they arrive there?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형을 변환하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: 소화 기관이 극적으로(dramatically) 줄어든다. drama(명사) → dramatically(부사).
det.analysis: shrink [부사] 구조. 동사 shrink를 수식하는 부사가 필요. drama(명사) → dramatic(형용사) → dramatically(부사).
det.tip: drama(명사) → dramatic(형용사) → dramatically(부사). 동사를 수식하려면 부사(-ly)를 써야 한다.

questions.passage: Well, most birds migrate after dark, including almost all of the birds that are normally active during the day. That's why it's hard for us to realize the migration is happening. They migrate at night because the night sky is cooler, and the air calmer. Besides, there are fewer __________ at night. If you could strip away the night sky and make everything visible, this migration would probably be the largest, greatest natural spectacle on the planet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밤에는 포식자(predators)가 더 적다. 새들이 밤에 이동하는 이유 중 하나.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ predators(포식자): 밤에 이동하는 이유로 '시원한 하늘, 잔잔한 공기'와 함께 '적은 포식자'를 언급
❌ ① spectators(관중): 이동과 무관
❌ ② companions(동반자): 밤에 적은 이유로 부적절
❌ ③ passengers(승객): 새의 이동 맥락에서 부적절
det.tip: predator = 포식자, 천적. 새들이 밤에 이동하는 3가지 이유: ① 시원한 하늘 ② 잔잔한 공기 ③ 적은 포식자

questions.passage: Oh, I had no idea that the Yellow Sea has such importance. What do you think we can do to preserve this precious gathering place for migratory birds? Well, you can start by raising __________ of its importance among people around you. Or, if you want to be more actively involved, you can participate in cleaning up beaches or monitoring wildlife habitats. On a bigger scale, because migratory birds travel through many countries, international cooperation is a must for their protection.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주변 사람들에게 그 중요성에 대한 인식(awareness)을 높이는 것부터 시작할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② awareness(인식/자각): 'raising awareness of its importance'는 중요성에 대한 인식을 높이다. 보전의 첫 걸음
❌ ① funds(자금): 문맥상 인식 제고가 먼저이고 자금 언급 없음
❌ ③ barriers(장벽): 장벽을 높이는 것은 보전과 모순
❌ ④ suspicion(의심): 의심을 높이는 것은 문맥에 부적절
det.tip: raise awareness = 인식을 높이다/제고하다. awareness of ~의 중요성에 대한 인식. conservation의 첫 단계
